title: Traversing Arrays with Loops
learningObjectives: Describe relevant storage, indexing and size rules.
Trace a collection operation or traversal.
Recognize bounds, lifetime or input pitfalls.
Apply the type to a practical collection task.

understand.concept: Traversal visits elements in sequence. Indexed loops expose position; range-based loops visit values directly when index is not needed.
understand.whyItMatters: Traversal is the basis of totals, searching, output and filtering.
understand.explain: Keep index bounds strict and trace each visited item.

examples.title: Range-for read
examples.explanation: No index is needed to read each element.

examples.title: Average
examples.explanation: Convert before division to keep fractional values.

examples.title: Reverse traversal
examples.explanation: A signed index counts down through valid indexes.

practise.guidedTask: Trace all five Traversing Arrays with Loops examples. Record sizes, indexes, values and condition checks. Identify first/last valid element and relevant edge cases.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ data-processing program demonstrating traversing arrays with loops. Test typical values, empty/boundary cases, and invalid input or indexing where relevant. Explain why this collection is appropriate.
hints: Use zero-based indexes and verify bounds.
Prefer range-based traversal when index is unnecessary.
Check emptiness before operations such as front or pop_back.
Test first, last and invalid boundaries.

questions.explanation: Start accumulator at a defined value.
Unsigned values wrap when decremented below zero.
